solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Changes plug when protecting point

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement, shortened to ad

indicators.note: protecting means one word wraps round and shields the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone adjusts an electrical plug while taking care to cover a sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plug' looks electrical but is the advertising sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to modify or alter it, a straight synonym of changes as a verb.

clue.text: Possibly Maradona's pass leading game

indicators.note: leading puts the first piece in front of the second

parts.note: to pass away is to die
Go is the ancient board game of black and white stones

explanation.surface: A footballer's pass sets up a match, the sort of thing said of Maradona.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition means Maradona's first name, with 'Possibly' marking it as one example of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego Maradona was the Argentine football star, so his forename is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Right gear boxing low in exercise

indicators.note: in places the combined letters inside the other word

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing one word inside another, as in a box

parts.note: rig is equipment or gear
low in the sense of base or despicable gives vile

explanation.surface: A gym-goer's proper kit includes something low-slung during exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is a noun here, an entitlement; 'boxing' and 'in' are two nested containers, the inner one inside the outer.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special entitlement, so it is a right enjoyed by some people.

clue.text: Cry of one eaten by ogre

indicators.note: eaten by means the first piece goes inside the ogre's name

parts.note: Shrek is the green ogre of the animated films
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A scream from a victim being devoured by a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: A shriek is a loud piercing cry, a synonym.

clue.text: Stuck time and time again, initially back hurt

indicators.note: back says those three opening letters are read in the reverse order
initially takes the first letter of each of the three words time, time and again

parts.note: ached means hurt, felt pain

explanation.surface: Someone has been stuck repeatedly, and at first their back hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives TTA and 'back' turns it to ATT; 'back' looks like a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Attached means fastened or fixed on, which is what stuck means here.

clue.text: Acts roughly about remarks about loveless refinement

indicators.note: the first about turns the abbreviation round

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly or approximately

indicators.note: the second about means the remarks go round the other piece

parts.note: comments are remarks

indicators.note: loveless removes O, the zero or love score in tennis

parts.note: polish is refinement or elegance

explanation.surface: A performance described as roughly about remarks concerning a lack of love and refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' appears twice with two jobs: first it reverses, then it contains. 'loveless' drops O, love being zero in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplishments are deeds achieved, so they are acts carried out successfully.

clue.text: Charm of Neandertal is manliness

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is drawn out from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A caveman's appeal lies in his manliness.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to bring luck, a lucky charm.

clue.text: Line complete following carbon copy

indicators.note: following puts line and complete after carbon

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
one can mean complete or united, as in 'all in one'

explanation.surface: Instructions for completing a line after making a carbon copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carbon copy' reads as one phrase but splits between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A clone is an exact replica, a copy of the original.

clue.text: Heartless enjoyment about joke over blokes making tackle

indicators.note: about means the outer letters go round the other pieces
heartless strips the word enjoyment of everything but its outer letters
over puts joke above blokes in this down clue

parts.note: a quip is a witty joke
men are blokes, British slang for chaps

explanation.surface: Fishermen with no joy, cracking jokes about each other's fishing tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackle' looks like a verb or a rugby move but is gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is the gear for a sport such as fishing, so equipment is a synonym.

clue.text: Cross cool redhead over mate pinching fabulous bird

indicators.note: over means the cool and redhead pieces are turned round

parts.note: to ice something is to cool it
the head of red is R

indicators.note: pinching means the mate grips the bird inside it

parts.note: pal is a mate or friend
the roc is the giant bird of Arabian fable

explanation.surface: An angry instruction to calm a ginger-haired friend who's stealing a mythical bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but is the adjective meaning mutual; 'over' turns ICER to RECI.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries give mutual or interchanged as an adjective sense of cross, which matches reciprocal, done in return by each side.

clue.text: Load of old paper rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the paper is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: A pile of old newspapers someone refused to take.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, a figurative load.

clue.text: Amphitheatre's unfinished pillar outside rises endlessly

indicators.note: outside means the shortened pillar wraps round the other piece
unfinished removes the last letter of the pillar

parts.note: a column is a pillar

indicators.note: endlessly removes both ends of the word rises

explanation.surface: An ancient arena's broken pillar is wrapped in endlessly rising stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay. 'unfinished' gives COLUM, 'endlessly' gives ISE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum or Coliseum in Rome is the most famous amphitheatre, and the word names any large arena.

clue.text: Starts to shut lids expecting easy peaceful slumber

definitions.text: Starts to shut lids expecting easy peaceful slumber

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of the six words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone begins to close their eyes, hoping for an easy, peaceful slumber.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone closing their eyelids in hope of peaceful rest is dozing off, as one does at night.

clue.text: Occasionally happy seen in part of church

indicators.note: occasionally takes only every other letter of the words happy seen

explanation.surface: Someone is now and then spotted looking cheerful at church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Natural to grab rising circus artist too early

indicators.note: to grab means the natural piece clutches the other inside it

parts.note: pure means natural or unadulterated

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a lion tamer is a circus performer

explanation.surface: A natural instinct to seize an ascending circus performer before it's needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses because this is a down clue; 'Natural' looks like the definition but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Premature means happening before the proper time, i.e. too soon.

clue.text: In a ferment, inclined to pen vacuous verse

indicators.note: to pen means to enclose, so the inclined piece encloses the other

parts.note: leaned means inclined or tilted

indicators.note: vacuous empties the word verse of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A poet in turmoil is disposed to write empty verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like writing but means enclose; 'In a ferment' is the definition, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavened dough has been raised by yeast, so it has been in a state of fermentation.

clue.text: Try continually to be outspoken on purpose

indicators.note: on places the spoken piece below purpose in this down clue

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose

indicators.note: outspoken signals that the word for continually is to be heard, not read

parts.note: ever means always, continually

explanation.surface: An exhortation always to speak your mind deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: The last syllables of the answer are said like 'ever'.
explanation.definitionFit: To endeavour is to attempt or strive, a synonym of try as a verb.

clue.text: Expedition, if far apart, returned carrying fuel

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
carrying means the words before it hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Members of an expedition that came home after splitting up were carrying fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'carrying fuel' as the definition, leaving the hiding unsignalled; 'carrying' is the hiding indicator and 'fuel' alone defines. 'returned' reads the hidden run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is a fuel, also called kerosene, burnt in lamps and heaters.

clue.text: Officers' abuse about Frenchman in retreat

indicators.note: in retreat means everything is read backwards
about means the abuse word goes round the name

parts.note: to slag someone off is to abuse them verbally, British slang
René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: Officers hurl insults at a Frenchman during a military withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is possessive, matching the answer read as officers'. 'in retreat' reverses the whole container, giving SLARENEG backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Generals are senior military officers.

clue.text: Girlfriend perhaps making trifle, flipping sweetheart

indicators.note: flipping turns the trifle word over, reading it backwards

parts.note: a tad is a trifle, a small amount
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A girlfriend prepares a trifle dessert, swearing at her sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifle' looks like the pudding; 'flipping' sounds like a mild curse.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is a person one goes out with romantically, of whom a girlfriend is one example.

clue.text: Fly tested twice, oddly

indicators.note: twice means the letters picked are written out two times
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word tested

explanation.surface: An insect was strangely tested twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting fly that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Sailor about to finish after crew's chant

indicators.note: after places the sailor piece behind the crew piece in the answer

parts.note: to crew a ship is to man it; the 's stands for 'is'

indicators.note: about to finish means the letter A (short for about) goes to the end of the sailor

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is close to ending the crew's song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' supplies A, the abbreviation, which moves to the end of TAR to give TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted repeatedly in meditation.

clue.text: Drunk's stash turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from the bottom, in reverse

parts.note: a depot is a store or stash

explanation.surface: An alcoholic's hidden supply has been found.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has', so the definition is drunk as a past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: To tope is to drink alcohol heavily, so toped means drunk as a verb form.

clue.text: Butcher's turning innocent, caught chopping horse

indicators.note: chopping means the other pieces cut into the horse word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: turning means the innocent word is read backwards

parts.note: an ass is a naive fool, an innocent
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A butcher turns innocent after being caught carving up a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is'. ASS is a palindrome, so 'turning' changes nothing visible.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre is to slaughter savagely, the verb sense of butcher.

clue.text: Get to behave hard for leader of Tories

indicators.note: for means hard takes the place of the other letter

parts.note: to react is to behave in response

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of Tories

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An instruction to make the Tory leader behave harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive at it, which is what get to means.

clue.text: Swallow, tailless bird with power

indicators.note: tailless docks the last letter of the bird

parts.note: a gull is a seabird
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A swallow is a bird that has lost its tail but still has power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird, keeping the bird theme, but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp is to swallow hurriedly.

clue.text: Running, nearly stumble, clutching ointment

indicators.note: clutching means the shortened stumble word holds the ointment inside
nearly cuts off the final letter of the stumble word

parts.note: to fall is to stumble
unction is an anointing oil or ointment

explanation.surface: A runner nearly trips while gripping a tube of ointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like the athlete's action but means working.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is running is operating, i.e. in working order.

clue.text: Horses without means to continue race?

definitions.text: Horses without means to continue race?

parts.words: Horses without means to continue race?
parts.note: castrated male horses lack the means to continue the breed, the race being their line of descent rather than a contest

explanation.surface: Racehorses unable to finish a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' looks like a horse race but means bloodline; castrated horses cannot breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Geldings are castrated male horses, which cannot sire offspring.

clue.text: Natural cordial, hot almost to the end

indicators.note: almost to the end means the hot letter moves to the next-to-last position

parts.note: hearty means cordial, warm and friendly
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A natural, warm drink that stays hot nearly to the last drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cordial' looks like the drink but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy means down-to-earth and unaffected, plain natural behaviour.
